day.note: Drew is almost certainly the Floofer. His partner is unclear, so the safest play is to lock in Drew.

Alex.confusing: How hugs work was the hardest part. I wasn't sure whether a Turkey that stays home would still be told it was hugged. I also couldn't tell whether I'd been hugged directly or for visiting the Floofer, because the report is the same either way. In round 3 that made my first read wrong.
Alex.fun: My favourite moment was round 3, when Blair and Ellis's egg counts made everything add up. I could publicly drop my own accusation, say sorry to Finley, and swing the table onto Drew in time.
Alex.change: I'd make the hug report say whether the Floofer visited you or you visited the Floofer. Right now one 'did nothing' message covers two situations that point to different suspects.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I opened by calling Finley the Floofer, assuming Ellis had been hugged. Instead I should have said 'I was hugged visiting Finley, so either he's the Floofer or the Floofer visited me' and waited for Ellis to confirm whether he was hugged.

Blair.confusing: In round 2, Finley went to -2 from being confused, even though nothing in the pool takes eggs. It wasn't clear how far off a wrong report can be, or whether it can make you discard. It also wasn't clear whether a Turkey, which stays home and takes no action, still gets told when it's hugged.
Blair.fun: In round 1, my Turkey claim was hard proof against Drew's fake Eagle claim. In round 3, the Turkey egg math (Casey at +1 instead of +2, Drew at +0) turned the whole table around.
Blair.change: Spell out exactly what a confused report does to egg counts. Also say whether roles that take no action get a hug notice, so the table isn't arguing over rules during the day.
Blair.regret: In round 2 as Meowfia, I gave up on Casey right away. Instead, I'd have used Finley's odd -2 and the Ellis/Drew double visit to raise doubt and try to split the vote, because the round was lost anyway. In the end I finished 1 point behind Ellis.

Casey.confusing: How a Turkey's eggs stack with a Falcon's own egg was easy to get wrong in the moment. I didn't see that a real Falcon visiting a Turkey who stayed home should end up +2, not +1.
Casey.fun: In round 1, Alex and I both reported being hugged at Drew, and the table locked onto the Floofer almost at once.
Casey.change: I'd show egg sources more clearly at dawn, such as "1 egg from a visit effect" versus "1 egg from your own role". Right now cats and Farm players alike misjudge the nest math, so a lot of the reasoning rests on guesswork.
Casey.regret: In round 3, I would take back the Falcon-on-Ellis claim, which didn't fit my +1, and my made-up rule that a Turkey isn't told it was hugged. I should have claimed a role whose numbers matched a single Turkey egg and stayed quieter, instead of drawing attention to myself.

Drew.confusing: Whether a Turkey, which stays home, gets the 'your animal did nothing' report when hugged. Round 3 hinged on that, and the table rule seemed to say yes, but I wasn't sure in the moment.
Drew.fun: In round 2 my Falcon report on Finley broke Casey's Eagle claim on the spot, and staking 25 points on that read paid off.
Drew.change: The Floofer is very hard to play: anyone who visits it gets a hug report, which points straight at the Floofer. I'd make visitors' hugs anonymous or optional so the cat isn't so easy to spot.
Drew.regret: In both Meowfia rounds my fake claim said I visited the player who turned out to be the Turkey, so my flat nest disproved it. I should have said I visited someone else, and not claimed to visit anyone until the egg changes had been discussed, so I could check the claim against the nest sizes.

Ellis.confusing: In round 3, Casey said a Turkey isn't told it was hugged because it doesn't act. The table rule says any hugged player is told, but the wording was loose enough for her to argue it, and the whole round depended on it.
Ellis.fun: Round 3. My being sure I wasn't hugged made Turkey egg-counting break both Drew's and Casey's claims, and Alex switched sides partway through the day.
Ellis.change: I would make the Wink easier to use well, or show players when it is the right moment. Without the order of speakers, it felt impossible to time.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I never used my Wink. I should have winked Blair early, since his Turkey claim was the strongest evidence against Drew. It might not have saved the round, but holding the Wink got us nothing.

Finley.confusing: In round 2 my confused Kookaburra report made me really discard 2 cards, even though nothing in the pool takes eggs. That -2 then counted against me in the nest totals and drew suspicion. It's hard to tell whether a confused egg count is meant to change your real nest.
Finley.fun: In round 2 Casey claimed to be the Eagle on Alex and said Alex had no visitors. I knew I had visited Alex myself, so that one fact broke Casey's claim.
Finley.change: I'd make confusion change only the information you're told, not your real nest. Then a Kookaburra who gets visited isn't losing real points for something nobody did.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I wrongly named Alex as Drew's partner. I should have said nothing about the second cat until the nest math was clear, because that math pointed at Casey.

review.title: The Turkey Always Talks
review.headline: Three rounds, three caught cats, and the Turkey's egg math broke every lie.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds, and each day ended by beat 2 or 3. In Round 1 Blair's Turkey broke Drew's fake Eagle claim. In Round 2 Drew's Falcon report broke Casey's Eagle claim. In Round 3 Alex wrongly accused Finley and Casey pushed for a 3-3 tie that would have eggsecuted a Farm player, but Ellis's Turkey math pulled everyone back onto Drew. Alex was Farm in all three rounds, never missed a vote, and won 85 to 67.

rounds.recap: Floofer Drew hugged Casey, and both Alex and Casey were hugged for visiting Drew, so two players reported hugs after visiting him. Drew claimed Eagle on Blair. Blair was the Turkey, and Drew's +0 nest disproved the visit. Everyone voted Drew. Ellis, the other cat, stayed hidden by throwing 0 at Drew.

Four players visited Finley, so the Kookaburra was confused and his wrong report made him discard 2 real cards. Casey claimed Eagle on Alex with no visitors. Finley's visit to Alex, confirmed by Drew's Falcon report, broke that claim. Blair's Tit claim was never checked, and Casey was eggsecuted with no pushback.

Drew claimed Tit on Ellis and Casey claimed Falcon on Ellis. Ellis was an unhugged Turkey, so Drew should have been +1, not +0, and Casey should have been +2, not +1. Alex first misread his own hug and accused Finley, and Casey backed him to set up a tie that would eggsecute Finley. Then Alex accepted the Turkey math and switched, and Drew was eggsecuted.

highlights.text: Blair's Turkey claim disproves Drew's Eagle visit with one fact: his nest stayed flat.
Drew's Falcon report places Finley at Alex, which breaks Casey's claim that she saw no visitors there as the Eagle.
Alex makes a confident case that Finley is the Floofer, and Casey quietly piles on to force a tie that would eggsecute a Farm player.
Blair and Ellis spell out that a Falcon visiting a working Turkey should be +2, which exposes Casey at +1, and Alex publicly reverses.

confusions.what: Picked a Falcon visit to the Turkey as her cover story, thinking it would explain a +1. Falcon's egg and the Turkey's egg stack, so the claim needed +2.

Concluded that Ellis had been hugged only because two visit claims didn't fit his eggs. He ignored that a hugged Turkey would be told so, and that he could have been the Floofer's direct target. This briefly framed Finley.
Claimed a visit to Ellis as a cover story without allowing for Ellis being the Turkey. A flat nest after visiting the Turkey exposed him, the same mistake he made with Blair in Round 1.

worked: Turkey: it turns any claimed visit into a public egg check. It caught a lie in Rounds 1 and 3 and produced the game's best deduction.
Public nest changes since the deal: every claim could be checked against a number, which kept the reasoning grounded and fair.
Falcon and Owl reports cross-checked each other. Drew's Falcon report in Round 2 confirmed Finley's visit and broke a cat's claim cleanly.
The tie-break rule (Farm player eggsecuted in a Farm-Meowfia tie) gave Casey a real plan in Round 3: a 3-3 split to eggsecute Finley.
problems: Meowfia never had a chance. Farm won 3/3, days ended early, no cat banked a card, and every cat threw 0. The winner was mostly decided by who got dealt Farm: Alex and Finley were Farm all three rounds. Fix: give cats a payoff for surviving the vote, or more ways to block information.

The house rule that hugged players are told makes the Floofer give itself away. Anyone who visits it learns they were hugged and says so, and this caught Drew in Rounds 1 and 3. Fix: tell only the Floofer's direct target, or stop hugging the Floofer's visitors.

Fake visit claims are too dangerous with a Turkey in the pool and public nest counts. Cats can't know who the Turkey is (only the Sphinx can find out), so any claimed visit can blow up. Fix: show cats which Farm animals are in play, or let a cat's safe animal come with a safe target.

Mouser's Wink was never used, in either Mouser round (Ellis in Round 1, Casey in Round 2). Days end so fast that it never gets a window. Fix: allow it at night or at the vote, or let it also cancel a vote.

A confused player draws or discards real cards based on a false report. Finley lost 2 real cards in Round 2 just because others visited him. Fix: apply the true egg count and make only the information wrong. Also clean up the log: blank Sphinx targets and duplicate 'no effect at tier' lines.
